title: Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiyya of Kfar Akko
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Moed Katan 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.16b.29), he speaks in the name of Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha.[^3]

Hyman places him in Tiberias, where Rabbi Ami lived, citing the incident in [Yevamot 45a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.45a.4): Rabbi Acha, the "officer of the Birah," and Rabbi Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiyya, a man of Kfar Akko, "ransomed captives who came from Armon to Tiberias" (and Rashi reads "to Antioch"); one of them had become pregnant by a gentile, and they came before Rabbi Ami, etc. And a few aggadic statements of his remain with us, as in [Taanit 7b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.7b.5), where he said: The rains are not withheld unless the enemies of Israel have become liable to destruction.

And in [Bekhorot 57b–58a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.57b.11-58a.1) he explains why they instituted separating the animal tithe at those three times: so that animals will be available for those who go up on the pilgrimage festivals.
And his death is mentioned in [Moed Katan 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25b.14): when he died, all the statues were cut down (according to the reading of Ein Yaakov and Dikdukei Soferim).

notes.text: The source has Armon and reports a Rashi reading Antioch. The death account follows the statue-cutting reading attributed to Ein Yaakov and Dikdukei Soferim.
“The enemies of Israel” is a euphemistic reference to Israel itself.

The first version in [Moed Katan 16b:29](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.16b.29) continues from Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha to Rabbi Simlai. Two other versions give Rabbi Tanchum citing Rav Huna, or Rav Huna speaking directly. The wording about the statues also appears in [Moed Katan 25b:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.25b.14).
